skill.name: device-management
skill.description: Manage UniFi device adoption, inventory, device status, and controller health across network infrastructure.

skill.author: DataKnifeAI

security_audit.summary: The external command findings are Markdown formatting false positives, and the API key finding is a placeholder rather than a hardcoded secret. The main security issue is the curl example that disables TLS certificate verification while sending an API key. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: The curl example disables TLS certificate verification while sending an API key.
remediation.suggestion: Remove -k from the command, or document trusted certificate setup before users send API credentials.
Tell users to keep UNIFI_API_KEY scoped, private, and out of prompts, logs, screenshots, and shared reports.

remediation.issue: Device inventory workflows expose sensitive infrastructure data.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should run inventory and adoption workflows only on UniFi networks they administer.

semantic_findings.title: TLS Certificate Verification Disabled in API Example
semantic_findings.description: The curl example uses -k while sending the UniFi API key header. This can expose credentials to interception if users copy the command on an untrusted network.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented command clearly disables TLS certificate validation while transmitting an API key. Legitimate self-signed controller use is possible, so severity is medium rather than high.

content.value_statement: UniFi teams need clear device status before adopting, tracking, or replacing hardware. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code organize inventory and controller health.
actual_capabilities: Lists UniFi devices that are pending adoption.
Lists adopted network devices for inventory work.
Retrieves device specifications, firmware, and status details.
Checks UniFi controller information and system status.
Explains how to handle empty UniFi site IDs.
Supports inventory reports and upgrade planning workflows.
limitations: Requires a configured UniFi MCP server and valid API access.
The documented tools are mostly read-oriented and do not show a direct adoption command.
Inventory quality depends on current UniFi controller data.
Curl examples may need trusted certificate configuration before use.

use_cases.title: Adopt New Network Hardware
use_cases.description: Find pending UniFi devices and prepare adoption notes by model, IP address, and planned role.

use_cases.title: Maintain Device Inventory
use_cases.description: Create a current inventory grouped by device type, location, firmware version, and operational status.

use_cases.title: Plan Hardware Refreshes
use_cases.description: Review device specifications and controller status to prioritize upgrades, replacements, and maintenance windows.

prompt_templates.title: Show Pending Devices
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check before onboarding new hardware.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use device-management to list devices pending adoption. Include MAC address, IP address, model, and recommended next action.

prompt_templates.title: Build Inventory Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine asset review for an existing UniFi network.
prompt_templates.prompt: List all adopted UniFi devices and group them by type. Include model, firmware, status, and any missing inventory details.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Controller Health
prompt_templates.scenario: Operational review before a maintenance window.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check UniFi controller information and summarize version, uptime, system status, and maintenance concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Lifecycle Actions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across inventory, adoption, and refresh needs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pending devices, adopted devices, device stats, and controller status. Produce a prioritized adoption and upgrade plan with risks.

output_examples.output: A concise pending-device list with MAC address, IP address, model, likely site, and recommended onboarding order.

output_examples.input: Create a device inventory report by type.
output_examples.output: An organized inventory summary grouped by access points, switches, gateways, and unknown devices, with firmware and status notes.
A prioritized refresh plan that highlights aging models, firmware gaps, controller health, and suggested maintenance windows.

best_practices: Use scoped UniFi API credentials and avoid sharing keys in prompts or reports.
Verify site IDs before comparing devices across multiple UniFi sites.
Document device purpose, location, and owner after every adoption workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not run device discovery against networks you do not administer.
Do not paste raw API keys, controller URLs, or full device identifiers into shared channels.
Do not treat inventory output as complete without checking controller sync status.

faq.question: What UniFi tasks does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports pending device review, adopted device inventory, device statistics, controller status, and planning workflows.

faq.question: Does it directly adopt devices?
faq.answer: The documented tools focus on listing and review. Confirm write-capable adoption tools before expecting direct adoption actions.

faq.question: Why can the site ID be empty?
faq.answer: UniFi APIs can return an empty site ID for the default site. The MCP server may resolve it automatically.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What access is required?
faq.answer: Users need a configured UniFi MCP server and authorized API credentials for the controller they manage.

faq.question: Is inventory data sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. Device names, MAC addresses, IP addresses, models, and firmware can reveal infrastructure details.
